## Configure R
This code will load the required R packages that RBEROST uses. To run the code, click the green triangle "Run Current Chunk" below. If no green arrow appears, and instead there is a red square, click the red square to stop any ongoing processes and a green triangle should appear in its place. When clicked, the green triangle will turn into a red square until the code is finished.

**Important:** Please open this project by double-clicking `Tier_1_Optimization-SSWR_5_3_2.Rproj` to ensure proper package management via renv.

The package installation may take several minutes the first time you run this code chunk. Follow any prompts that appear in the R console to complete package installation.
You may need to use renv::install("package_name") to manually install any packages that fail to install automatically. When renv::status() shows that all packages are installed, proceed to the next code chunk.

Y
```{r configureR}

# Check renv status to ensure all packages are installed
renv::status()

# If packages are missing, restore the environment from the renv package list
renv::restore()

# If any packages are still missing, manually install them using renv::install("package_name")
# Example: renv::install("tidyverse") # Comment out or remove this line after installing the package

```

## Load all required packages
This code chunk will load all required R packages. To run the code, click the green triangle.
If there are any errors indicating that a package is not installed, please refer to the previous code chunk to install missing packages.

```{r loadpackages}
# Load required packages
library(tidyverse)
library(units)
library(dplyr)
library(measurements)
library(reshape2)
library(data.table)
library(stringr)
library(foreach)
library(shiny)
library(shinycssloaders)
library(tidygraph)
library(bit64)
library(beepr)
library(rneos)
library(doParallel)
library(magrittr)
```
## Download lfs files from Zenodo (required unless using git lfs to download large files)

When you download the repository from github, only placeholders for large files (>100MB) listed
in the .gitattributes file will be downloaded.  If you are using git you can install lfs and
download these in git.  Otherwise, you can download these files directly from a Zenodo archive
by cutting and pasting each of the following urls into a browser (or pointing to each of the urls below and using (<Ctrl-Click>) and saving each into the .\RBEROSTV2D\RBEROST-Pacific\Preprocessing\Inputs folder then unzipping to that folder.  Don't create additional subdirectories under Inputs when unzipping any .zip files.  If those links time out then navigate to https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19185509 and click on corresponding buttons to download each file.

https://zenodo.org/record/21923766/files/data_puget1.zip?download=1
https://zenodo.org/record/21923766/files/pac_sparrow_model_input.zip?download=1
https://zenodo.org/record/21923766/files/predict_puget_tn.zip?download=1
https://zenodo.org/record/21923766/files/predict_puget_tp.zip?download=1
https://zenodo.org/record/21923766/files/RiparianEfficiencies_update.zip?download=1

## Run SSM Model Vintage Comparison
To run the SSM Model Vintage Comparison, ensure the two versions of the Salish Sea Model shapefiles are in the preprocessing folder and then execute the following code chunk:

**Important** : You must set the working directory variable in this code chunk even if you do not intent to use the mapper. The working_dir variable is used in later code chunks.

```{r ssmcompare}

# This variable represents the working directory where RBEROST is located. 
# You will need to write out the full path ending with the "RBEROSTV2D/" folder.
working_dir <- "C:/Users/ndetenbe/OneDrive - Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)/RBEROSTV2D/"

# Do not change anything below this line --------------------------------------------------------------
setwd(working_dir)
source(paste0(working_dir, "RBEROST-Pacific/R/00_PreprocessSalishSeaVintageMapper_V3.R"), local = TRUE)
Salish_Sea_Mapper

```

# This variable determines what watersheds/targets will be included in the model.
watershed_choices <- c("Nisqually R")

# Select years to include in the model 2008 (4) avg year 2011 (7) wet 2019 dry (15)
model_years <- c("6","7") #, "2", ..., "16"

# Load parameter specification
actionable_load <- TRUE # If TRUE, the model will exclude "other" loads from sources such as snowmelt and atmospheric deposition for which there are no applicable BMPs that can reduce them
# Note: Setting to FALSE is much more likely to result in infeasible results since "other" loads typically make up sizeable portions of overall loadings within a watershed, and as such the reduction target percentages exceed the amount that can be reduced by BMPs in other categories. 

# This variable represents to expected interest rate. Default is 0.03, or 3%.
interest_rate <- 0.03

# This variable lets the user decide if they wish to consider agricultural BMP efficiencies of practices versus "No Practice" (a default of no conservation practices) or "Baseline" (a default of practices currently in place, and implementing a BMP will remove practices currently in place).
AgBMPcomparison <- "No Practice"

# This variable decides if you will run RBEROST with or without uncertainty. It can be TRUE or FALSE. Running with uncertainty takes longer than running without.
IncludeUncertainty <- FALSE

# If running RBEROST with uncertainty, how many scenarios would you like to view? Default is 3.
n.scenarios <- 1 

# If running RBEROST with uncertainty, how different would you like the scenarios to be? Each scenario will be solved for loading limits that are a certain percentage lower than the previous. Default is 0.20, or 20%.
scenariostepchange <- 0.01

# ----- Do not change anything below this line -------
suppressWarnings({
setwd(working_dir)
})

# Create year crosswalk that will be used to filter dataframes that use YYYY format
year_xwalk <- data.frame(c(1:16), c(2005:2020))
colnames(year_xwalk) <- c("model_year", "year")
year_xwalk <- year_xwalk %>%
  filter(model_year %in% model_years)

year_filter <- as.numeric(unique(year_xwalk$year))

invisible(source(paste0(working_dir, "RBEROST-Pacific/R/Optimization_HelperFunctions-Pacific.R")))

# source urban and road cost estimate code to calculate costs using selected time period
if (!exists("final_cost_data") | !exists("final_effic_data")) {
  invisible(source(paste0(working_dir, "RBEROST-Pacific/R/00_CostandEffic_Calc_ND.R")))
} #*# updated for 2025USD and 99%ile cost threshold
if (!exists("road_data") | !exists("road_effic_data") | !exists("road_area")) {
  invisible(source(paste0(working_dir, "RBEROST-Pacific/R/00_ProcessRoadBMPsND.R")))
} #*# updated for 2025USD

source(

  local = TRUE
  )

## Define auto upload functions
This code chunk will define variables and run the NEOS optimization script. To run the code, click the green triangle "Run Current Chunk" below. If no green arrow appears, and instead there is a red square, click the red square to stop any ongoing processes and a green triangle should appear in its place. When clicked, the green triangle will turn into a red square until the code is finished.
This will automatically upload the model files created in the preprocessor to the NEOS server for optimization.
Note: The code uses the default file names from the pre-processor. If you have changed the command, model, or data file names from the default names it will not process those files.

```{r autoupload}

# Variables for User to Update ------------------------------------------------

# Enter valid email address
email <- "detenbeck.naomi@epa.gov"

# Enter a filepath where the NEOS result file will be saved.
# If you have not changed the folder structure, you should not need to change this variable.
NEOSresults <- paste0(working_dir, "RBEROST-Pacific/Preprocessing/Outputs/")

# Automatically define file name suffix with watershed choice name and date for results
paramname <- paste0(paste(watershed_choices, collapse = "_"), "_", Sys.Date())

# Comments for NEOS run
comments <- "Nisqually R wet year"

# Run NEOS optimization script-----------------------------------------------
suppressWarnings({
setwd(working_dir)
})
source(paste0(working_dir, "RBEROST-Pacific/R/01_Optimization_NEOSInteraction-Pacific.R"))

# This will notify you when preprocessing is complete, users may delete if not desired.
beepr::beep() #*#
```


## Run Postprocessor
To run the postprocessor, click the green triangle below. A window will pop up either in RStudio or in your default web browser. If no green arrow appears, and instead there is a red square, click the red square to stop any ongoing processes and a green triangle should appear in its place. When clicked, the green triangle will turn into a red square until the code is finished. Be aware that simply closing the browser window will not stop the Shiny app. You must also click the red square below if you wish to relaunch the app.

```{r runpostprocessor}
suppressWarnings({
setwd(working_dir)
})
options(shiny.maxRequestSize = 100000 * 1024^2)
source(paste0(working_dir, "RBEROST-Pacific/R/02_Optimization_RunShiny-Pacific_ICF24_V5.R"), local = TRUE)
```
